AccessLevel.description:
How much a person may do with a resource. Each level includes the ones below it, so compare
levels: `access >= AccessLevel.Write`. What a level allows for its own data, each module
decides.

plan.description:
Whether it is a plan: a person's subscription, added by signing in at its vendor and only ever
their own. Otherwise it is an API key, added with its secret, a workspace's or someone's own.

allowed.description: Whether this host allows adding it.

AgentAccountKindSummary.description: A kind of account as this host offers it.

kind.description: What it is at its vendor.

name.description: Its name for people, such as `Team key`.

oneOf.description: The workspace whose people with Write use it, for a workspace's account.
The person it belongs to, for a personal account.

endpoint.description: The API's base URL for an API key at another endpoint than the vendor's; otherwise `null`.

needsSignIn.description:
Whether the account's sign-in ended, such as a ChatGPT plan whose owner disconnected the app in
ChatGPT: it runs no agents until it is removed and added again.

AgentAccountSummary.description:
An agent account as people see it; its secret is never shown. A workspace's account has a
WorkspaceId; a person's own has an OwnerId.

repositories.description: Their names, such as `acme/api`, and whether each is private.

installUrl.description: Where the person installs the app on more accounts or repositories.

AvailableRepositories.description:
The repositories a person's GitHub connection reaches: those of the accounts and organizations the
host's GitHub App is installed on that the person may see.

private.description: Whether only people given access see it.

AvailableRepository.description: A repository a person's GitHub connection reaches.

files.description: The files changed, added, removed, or renamed.

ChangeCount.description: How much a nook's repositories changed since they were copied in, all of them together.

calls.description: How many calls its agents made then.

cost.description: What they cost in US dollars, as far as their prices are known.

estimate.description: Whether the cost is a plan's estimate at the vendor's API prices.

ChatCost.description: What one chat's model calls cost over some days.

ChatEventBody.description:
What happened in a chat. A message is sent, then either starts a turn, goes into the running
turn (steered), or is cancelled. A turn shows the agent's updates and ends with a stop reason,
then a checkpoint of the nook's files. A proposal stays with the people in the chat until the
account's owner sends it on. An agent that had to be started again says whether it remembers.
Someone may change the agent's model or account, from the next turn on.
The nook's setup, when its files have one, starts and ends before its agent starts; someone may ask
to run it again, which it does once the agent answered what was sent before, or start a chat that
fixes it. When AiSloth's own work on the chat keeps failing, the chat says so until it goes on.

isProposal.description: Whether it is a proposal: it never reaches the agent, and the account's owner may send it on.

ChatMessage.description: A message someone sent to a chat.

nookId.description: The nook its agent works in.

working.description: Whether the agent is working on a turn, or messages wait for it.

harness.description: The harness that runs its agent.

model.description:
The model its agent runs on from its next turn; `null` only for a chat started before
every chat had one, which takes one (Task<Result<ChatSummary>> IChatsApi.ChangeModelAsync(Actor actor, ChangeModel command, CancellationToken ct)) before its next message.

thinking.description: How hard its agent thinks from its next turn.

account.description: The agent account that pays for its work from its next turn.

oneOf.description:
The owner of the personal account it runs on, whose messages alone reach the agent: everyone
else's are proposals. `null` on the workspace's account, which people with Write
on the workspace use.

title.description:
What the chat is about, as lists show it: the first line of its first message, at most 80
characters; `null` until someone writes in it.

oneOf.description: The chat whose conversation it continues (bool StartChat.WithConversation), if any.

ChatSummary.description: A chat as the people with access to its nook see it.

calls.description: How many calls the chat's agents made.

cost.description: What they cost in US dollars, as far as their prices are known; null when none is.

estimate.description: Whether the cost is a plan's estimate at the vendor's API prices.

contextUsed.description: Tokens in the context at the latest call, its input and answer.

contextWindow.description: The most tokens the chat's model's context holds, when known.

cacheWarmUntil.description: Until when the prompt's cache stays, at least, when a call used one and the vendor's rule is known.

rereadCost.description: What the next call costs to read the context again once the cache is gone, in US dollars, when known.

turns.description: The latest turns' usage, newest first, at most 50.

ChatUsage.description:
What a chat's agents have used of their models: every call the model gateway saw, added up and by
turn, with what a cost is known for; how full the context is; and how long its prompt's cache stays.

number.description: Its number in the nook, counting from 1.

note.description: What it follows, in words for people.

oneOf.description:
How much its repositories had changed since they were copied in, kept with it; `null`
when it didn't keep them.

CheckpointSummary.description: A nook's files as they were at one moment, kept while the nook exists.

coAuthor.description: The trailer that credits AiSloth, such as `Co-authored-by: AiSloth <…>`, or `null`.

CommitIdentity.description:
Who commits in a person's nooks name: the author and the committer, and the co-author line added to
every message, if any.

day.description: The day, in the time zone asked for.

cost.description: What they cost in US dollars, as far as their prices are known.

estimate.description: Whether the cost includes plans' estimates at the vendors' API prices.

DayUsage.description: What one day's model calls in a workspace used and cost.

GitHubAccount.description: A person's GitHub account, connected to AiSloth.

GitHubConnectionAttemptId.description: Identifies a person's attempt to connect their GitHub account.

oneOf.description: The connected account; `null` while the person hasn't approved yet.

retryAfter.description: How long to wait before completing again, while waiting.

GitHubConnectionProgress.description: Where a GitHub connection stands: connected, or still waiting for the person.

userCode.description: What the person enters at GitHub, such as `WDJB-MJHT`.

interval.description: How long to wait between completions.

GitHubConnectionStarted.description:
A GitHub connection waiting for the person: they open VerificationUri, enter
UserCode, and approve; meanwhile the caller completes it every
Interval until it is connected or expires.

name.description: The name: 1 to 100 characters, without `<`, `>`, or line breaks.

email.description: The email address, such as GitHub's no-reply address for the account.

GitIdentity.description: Who a commit names, as git writes it: `Name <email>`.

oneOf.description: Who commits name as their author; `null` for the person's GitHub account.
Who commits name as their committer; `null` for the author.

aiSlothCoAuthor.description: Whether every commit credits AiSloth as its co-author.

branchPrefix.description: What branches AiSloth names start with, such as `aisloth/`; a push can name any branch instead.

oneOf.description:
What commits get, with the defaults filled in; `null` while the author comes from a
GitHub account the person hasn't connected.

GitSettings.description: How a person's commits and branches look. Their choices, and what those amount to.

GrantSummary.description: Someone given access to a resource directly, not through what it is in.

id.description: Its ID at the account's vendor, such as `openai/gpt-6-luna`.

name.description: Its name for people, as the vendor gives it.

thinkingLevels.description:
The harness's thinking levels the model takes, in the harness's words, lightest first; empty when
the model doesn't reason, so no level applies.

facts.description: What's known of it at the account: its limits, its price, and its cache's lifetime.

HarnessModel.description: A model a harness can run on with an account, as a chat's model.

shared.description:
Whether it is the workspace's, kept from the chats on the workspace's accounts and given to all of
them, rather than the actor's own, kept from the chats on their own accounts.

savedAt.description: When a chat last saved it.

oneOf.description: The chat that saved it last, unless that chat is gone.

HarnessStateSummary.description: Harness state for one harness, as the list of a workspace's harness state shows it.

id.description: What a nook takes as its harness, such as `claude-code`.

accepts.description: The kinds of agent account it can run on.

thinkingLevels.description: How hard it can think, in its own words, such as `high`, lightest first.

defaultThinking.description: The level, one of its levels, a new chat thinks at unless someone chooses another.

HarnessSummary.description: A harness chats can run, and the agent accounts it takes.

workspace.description: The workspace's, for everyone's chats there.

personal.description: The person's own, for the chats they start.

Instructions.description:
What every agent of a person's chats in a workspace is told to follow, besides each repository's
own instructions: the workspace's first, then the person's own. Empty for none.

code.description: The one-time code to pass on.

Invite.description:
A new invite: whoever accepts Code first gets the access, once, until it expires.
The code is shown only here.

LinkCode.description: A code that signs its creator in on another device, once, until it expires. Shown only here.

code.description: Registers the machine once; never shown again.

MachineRegistration.description:
A machine just added, with the one-time code that registers it:
`sloth machine connect <control plane> <code>` on the machine.

MachineStatus.description: Whether a machine can run nooks right now.

workspaceId.description: The workspace whose nooks it runs.

status.description: Whether it can run nooks right now.

MachineSummary.description: A machine as the people with access to its workspace see it.

MessageId.description: Identifies a message in a chat.

ModelAccessKind.description:
A way to pay for a vendor's models: an API key, added with its secret, or a person's plan, signed in
as the vendor's own agent signs in. Stored by name.

efforts.description:
The reasoning efforts it takes, in its vendor's words, such as `low` and `high`; empty when
it takes a thinking budget or a switch instead, or doesn't reason.

contextWindow.description: The most tokens its context holds.

maxOutput.description: The most tokens it writes in one answer.

oneOf.description: What its tokens cost at this account.

cacheLifetime.description:
How long the vendor keeps a prompt's cache after its last use, at least: Anthropic's five minutes,
OpenAI's five, or thirty for its newest models.

ModelFacts.description:
What's known of a model at an account: from the account's vendor, where it says, and otherwise from
models.dev's open catalog. What isn't known is `null`, never a guess.

input.description: Each input token not read from a cache.

cacheRead.description: Each input token read from a cache, when the vendor prices it apart.

cacheWrite.description: Each input token written to a cache, when the vendor prices it apart.

tiers.description: Higher prices for calls with more input than each tier's threshold, lowest first.

estimate.description: Whether it's a plan's estimate at the vendor's API prices rather than a price paid.

ModelPrice.description:
What a model's tokens cost, in US dollars per million: what an API key pays its vendor, or, for a
plan, which pays no price per token, what the same tokens would cost at the vendor's API.

branch.description: The branch to start from, or `null` for its default branch.

NookRepository.description: A repository a new nook starts with.

scripts.description: The scripts, as paths in the nook's files, in the order they run; empty when there are none.

oneOf.description: Their latest run, or `null` when there are no scripts.

readyCopyMadeAt.description:
When the ready copy the latest run set the nook up from was made: a copy of a nook with the same
files right after a setup that took a while, which leaves this setup little to do. `null`
when the run set it up from scratch, or only resumed it.

NookSetup.description:
A nook's setup: scripts that come with its files and prepare it, which run whenever the nook gets
its files, as a new nook, a copy, or one brought back after its sandbox was lost. Every
`.agents/setup` runs first, installing what the code needs, then every `.agents/resume`,
starting its services; those at the top of the files before each folder's directly in it, by
name, each in its own folder, with the workspace's secrets. A setup may take 30 minutes and
a resume 5. Their output is also written to `/var/log/aisloth/setup.log` in the nook.

name.description: Its name, which is its folder in `/work`.

repository.description: The workspace's repository it is a copy of.

branch.description: The branch it started from; `null` for the default branch until it's copied in.

commit.description: The commit it started from, the base of its changes; `null` until it's copied in.

NookSource.description: A repository in a nook, at `/work/<name>`.

NookStatus.description:
Where a nook is in its lifecycle, as people see it. Callers never have to act on it: any operation
wakes an asleep nook and waits for a starting one, so callers only notice latency.

provider.description: The ID of the provider it runs on, as in string ProviderSummary.Id.

status.description: Where it is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: What it uses of its disk, memory, and CPU while it runs; `null` while it doesn't.

diskNearlyFull.description:
Whether its disk is so full that its work, and keeping its files as checkpoints, may soon fail:
people should free space, or move to a nook with a bigger disk.

image.description: The image it started from, such as one with a chat's harness, or `null` for the base image.

oneOf.description:
The one person who may change what runs in it or its files, such as the owner of the personal
account its chat's agent works on; `null` for everyone with Write on its workspace.

sources.description: Its sources, each a repository at `/work/<name>`, by name.

NookSummary.description: A nook as the people with access to it see it.

diskUsedBytes.description: The disk space the nook's files use.

cpuUsedMillicores.description: The CPU its processes used since the last measurement, in thousandths of a core.

cpuTotalMillicores.description: The CPU it may use, in thousandths of a core.

NookUsage.description:
How much of its disk, memory, and CPU a nook uses, as its daemon last measured it, every 30
seconds while it runs. A figure its daemon can't measure is 0. On the Docker provider the disk is
the host's, because Docker can't cap a container's disk on most setups.

items.description: The items, in the list's stable order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it in the next PageRequest; `null` on the last page.

PageOfChatSummary.description: One page of a keyset-paginated list.

items.description: The items, in the list's stable order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it in the next PageRequest; `null` on the last page.

PageOfCheckpointSummary.description: One page of a keyset-paginated list.

items.description: The items, in the list's stable order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it in the next PageRequest; `null` on the last page.

PageOfNookSummary.description: One page of a keyset-paginated list.

items.description: The items, in the list's stable order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it in the next PageRequest; `null` on the last page.

PageOfProcessSummary.description: One page of a keyset-paginated list.

items.description: The items, in the list's stable order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it in the next PageRequest; `null` on the last page.

PageOfWorkspaceSummary.description: One page of a keyset-paginated list.

meters.description:
Each limit or count the vendor reports, in its order; empty for an account that isn't a plan, or a
plan whose vendor has reported none yet.

reportedAt.description: When the vendor reported them; null when nothing was reported.

PlanUsage.description: What a plan has used of its limits, as its vendor reports it.

name.description: Its name for people, such as `pi · GPT-6 Luna`.

harness.description: The harness that runs the agent.

account.description: The agent account that pays for its work.

model.description: The model its agent runs on.

PresetSummary.description:
A person's saved choice of how a chat runs, a shortcut when they start one: a harness, the agent
account that pays, the model, and how hard it thinks.

aboveInputTokens.description: The threshold, counting every input token, cached or not.

input.description: Each input token not read from a cache.

cacheRead.description: Each input token read from a cache.

cacheWrite.description: Each input token written to a cache.

PriceTier.description: The prices of calls with more input tokens than AboveInputTokens.

ProcessEvent.description:
Something a running process did: wrote output, or exited. A process's events arrive in order,
and ProcessExited is always its last.

ProcessId.description: Identifies a process in a nook. The control plane creates it before the daemon starts the process.

startedAt.description: When the control plane asked the daemon to start it.

exitCode.description: Its exit code, or `null` while it runs.

id.description: What string CreateNook.Provider takes; callers don't parse it.

name.description:
Its display name: `cloud` for the deployment's own provider, whatever runs it, or each one's
own name, such as `docker`, when a deployment runs several, as in development; a machine's name
for a machine.

available.description: Whether it can create nooks right now; a machine that is offline can't.

ProviderSummary.description:
A provider a workspace's nooks can run on: one the deployment runs for every workspace, such as a
Docker Engine or a cloud, or one of the workspace's own machines.

RepositoryId.description: Identifies a repository a workspace connected.

name.description: Its folder in a nook, the repository's own name, such as `api`.

fullName.description: Its name on GitHub, such as `acme/api`.

defaultBranch.description: The branch nooks start from unless told otherwise, which AiSloth never pushes to.

RepositorySummary.description: A repository a workspace connected, which its nooks can start with at `/work/<name>`.

id.description: Its ID, in the module that owns it.

Resource.description:
Something people are given access to: a workspace or a nook. Access to a resource reaches what is
in it, so a workspace's editor writes in all its nooks.

ResourceKind.description: The kinds of Resource people can be given access to.

id.description: The secret; replacing its value keeps it.

workspaceId.description: The workspace whose nooks get it.

setAt.description: When its value was set last.

SecretSummary.description: A secret as people see it: never its value.

SessionId.description: Identifies a session: one signed-in device.

device.description: What the device is, such as `sloth on alex-laptop`.

lastUsedAt.description: When it was last used, to the day.

SessionSummary.description: A signed-in device, without its token.

process.description: The process, to watch its output.

endedAt.description: When it ended, or `null` while it runs.

exitCode.description: How it ended, or `null` while it runs: 0 when every script succeeded.

SetupRun.description:
A run of a nook's setup scripts: one process, whose output says what each script did. It fails
with the first failing script's exit code, 124 for one that ran out of time, after the others ran.

retryAfter.description: How long to wait before completing it again, while there is no account.

SignInProgress.description:
How a sign-in stands: the account, once added; until then, the person hasn't approved its code yet,
and the caller completes it again after RetryAfter.

userCode.description: What the person enters there, such as `WDJB-MJHT`, for a sign-in with a code.

expiresAt.description: When the sign-in can no longer complete.

interval.description: How long to wait before completing a sign-in with a code; zero otherwise.

SignInStarted.description:
A sign-in in progress, until ExpiresAt: the person opens Url.
With a UserCode (a Copilot plan, at GitHub; a ChatGPT plan, at OpenAI), they
enter it there and approve, while the caller completes the sign-in every Interval
until it is done. Without one (a Claude plan), they approve there and bring back the code the page
shows, which the caller completes the sign-in with, once.

source.description: The source, by name: the repository is at `/work/{Source}`.

repository.description: The workspace's repository the source is a copy of.

baseBranch.description: The branch it was copied in from.

baseCommit.description: The commit it was copied in at, which the changes are against.

patch.description:
The changes as `git diff` prints them, one section per changed file, its commits since and
what isn't committed together, new files included; empty without changes. A binary file's
section says only that it differs.

truncated.description:
Whether the patch leaves out files at its end, because all of them would be more than
int SourceChanges.MaxPatch bytes; it never ends inside a file.

SourceChanges.description: What one of a nook's repositories changed since it was copied in.

input.description: Input tokens neither read from a cache nor written to one.

cacheRead.description: Input tokens read from a cache.

cacheWrite.description: Input tokens written to a cache, for minutes or an hour.

reasoning.description: Of the output, the reasoning tokens.

TokenCounts.description: Tokens of model calls, added up; input counted once, as in ModelCallUsage.

cost.description: What they cost in US dollars, as far as their prices are known.

estimate.description: Whether the cost is a plan's estimate at the vendor's API prices.

TurnUsage.description: What one turn's model calls used and cost.

name.description: What it counts, as people read it, such as `5 hours`, `Week`, `Week, Opus`, `Premium requests`, or `Credits`.

used.description: How much is used: a percent of a window, a count of a quota, the credits spent.

limit.description: The most it allows, in the same unit: 100 for a window; null for spend without a limit.

resetsAt.description: When it starts over, when the vendor says.

UsageMeter.description: One of a plan's limits or counts: a window, a quota, or spend without a limit.

UserId.description: Identifies a user. It lives in Foundation, not in a module, because Actor needs it.

UserProfile.description: A user as they see themselves.

UserSummary.description: A user as others see them.

access.description: How much the caller may do in it.

WorkspaceSummary.description: A workspace as one person with access sees it.

days.description: Each day, the oldest first, days without calls included.

chats.description: Each chat with calls in those days, with what they cost, the costliest first.

calls.description: How many calls all of them made.

cost.description: What they cost in US dollars, as far as their prices are known.

estimate.description: Whether the cost includes plans' estimates at the vendors' API prices.

WorkspaceUsage.description:
What a workspace's chats used of their models over its last days, from every call the model gateway
saw.
